title: Run a command on each file in a folder with a safe loop
summary: Go through a list of files or lines one item at a time and do something with each. The read settings keep spaces, backslashes and leading blanks intact, so a name such as my report.txt is handled correctly.

aliases.text: loop over lines of command output bash
for each file run command bash loop
process each file in folder bash script
цикл по строкам вывода команды bash
обработать каждый файл в папке в цикле
while read с пробелами в именах bash

steps.explain: find -print0 ends each name with a zero byte, so spaces survive. IFS= and -r keep each name exactly as it is, and -d '' ends each read at the zero byte. The loop body counts the lines of each file.
steps.cmd: find <DIR> -type f -name '*.<EXT>' -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' FILE; do printf '%6s lines  %s\n' "$(wc -l < "$FILE")" "$FILE"; done
steps.expect: One line per file, for example '    12 lines  notes/my report.txt'.

steps.explain: Read a plain list of lines, one at a time. IFS= keeps leading and trailing spaces, -r keeps backslashes as they are, and printf prints each line without interpreting it.
steps.cmd: while IFS= read -r LINE; do printf 'item: %s\n' "$LINE"; done < <LIST_FILE>
steps.expect: One line per input line, each starting with item:

placeholders.name: LIST_FILE
placeholders.description: A text file with one item per line

source.title: Bash Reference Manual: Bash Builtin Commands (read)
